A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The original experimental Appendix E maps to Appendix F in v2; v2 adds a separate theoretical Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on synthetic problems, LIBSVM classification datasets, and CIFAR datasets, including additional results and sensitivity experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original optimization experiments and reports revised deep-learning results in Section 4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The three main SHB algorithms and their step-size recurrences remain unchanged. Appendix E adds a limited procedural extension: projected IMA projects the auxiliary z update onto a compact convex domain while retaining the existing averaging operation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic least-squares and logistic-regression problems, LIBSVM vowel/letter/vehicle/glass, and CIFAR-10/100 classification. Changed architecture–dataset pairings remain within this coverage. The new constrained optimization formulation is not empirically evaluated.

E2.justification: The optimizer comparator sets are retained across the corresponding deterministic, stochastic, and decreasing-step-size experiments, including ALR-MAG/ALR-SMAG, Adam, naive-momentum SPSmax, and AdaGrad-Norm. Newly displayed naive-momentum training-loss traces concern an already evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported ResNet experiments change from 200 to 100 epochs, as shown in Figures 5, 6, and 19 and Table 3. Figure 20 replaces DenseNet121 on CIFAR-10 with ResNet18 on CIFAR-100; ResNet18 already appeared in v1 Figure 19. These substantially revise the deep-learning budgets and model configurations, while batch size and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The momentum sensitivity, alternative correcting-factor placement, step-size-bound comparisons, and convergence-constant analyses are retained in Figures 8–14, moving from Appendix E to F. Cases omitted from the shortened Figure 1 remain in Figure 9. The new projection appendix adds theory rather than an empirical robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five trials in Tables 2 and 3 and retain the mean/standard-deviation reporting practice. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Deep-learning curves in Figures 5, 6, and 19 are replaced, and Figure 20 reports a different architecture–dataset pairing. ALR-SMAG changes from divergent loss and near-chance ResNet34 test accuracy in v1 to successful learning in v2. These are revised outcomes under changed settings, not evidence of a matched-setting performance gain. The convex and sensitivity results are largely retained.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces constrained optimization, projection non-expansiveness, and projected-IMA convergence Theorems E.2–E.3 with proof arguments. v2 also corrects the telescoping calculation leading to Equation 20, revises Definition C.2's smoothness characterization, and changes the constant-step-size bound denominator from T gamma_b to T gamma. The original unconstrained bounded-iterates assumption remains.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims about three adaptive SHB step sizes, non-interpolated convergence, exact convergence for decreasing variants, and recovery of SGD guarantees without momentum. The added appendix and removal of the concluding recap do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 removes the DNN interpretation that both ALR-SMAG and naive momentum diverge and thereby demonstrate the benefit of the proposed balancing mechanism. Appendix E adds a substantive qualification: its bounded-iterates workaround uses compact-domain projection, and projected IMA is not necessarily equivalent to projected SHB.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies c=0.4 for MomSPSmax in the DNN experiments and c=0.1 for ALR-SMAG in Appendix F.7. v1 did not explicitly disclose these method-specific DNN values, so their disclosure alone does not establish a parameter change. Hardware and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction, Section 2.2, Table 1, and Appendix A replace the interpolation-only characterization of Wang et al. with a distinction between adaptive moving-averaged-gradient momentum and SHB. v2 also discusses differences in their zero-momentum guarantees, adds Garrigos and Gower's projection reference, and removes the DenseNet citation. The broader literature coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain intact. v2 makes localized wording edits, converts experiment subsections to run-in headings, names existing assumptions and corollaries, and removes Conclusion and Future Work. Some formerly explicit IMA references become the less clear wording '2.3 method'.

P2.justification: The ICLR format substantially changes typography, text width, figure sizing, and placement. Figures 1–2 are wrapped into text; Figure 1 is reduced from four panels to two, with the other cases retained in Figure 9. Figures 3–6 become smaller side-by-side displays with shortened captions, and the revised DNN plots have changed axes and legends.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit DNN parameters, corrects the D.2 derivation, and adds a constrained projection extension with explicit scope limits. Its DNN discussion also better matches the revised ALR-SMAG curves. These gains outweigh the reduced architectural breadth and smaller, less legible plots, but do not resolve the bounded-iterates limitation for the original unconstrained SHB methods or establish performance improvements under matched settings.
